S-EE-001.cause: Missing or insufficient authentication and validation of external entities
S-EE-001.attack: Attacker impersonates a trusted external entity by sending forged requests, bypassing identity checks, or reusing stolen credentials

S-P-001.threat: Unauthorized process access via identity spoofing
S-P-001.cause: Weak or missing authentication mechanisms for process access
S-P-001.attack: Attacker spoofs a legitimate identity to gain unauthorized access to a protected process

S-P-002.threat: Process spoofing via malicious process replacement
S-P-002.cause: Lack of process integrity verification or trust validation
S-P-002.attack: Attacker replaces a legitimate process with a malicious one using the same identifier or interface

S-P-003.cause: Improper session management or weak session binding
S-P-003.attack: Attacker takes over a valid user session by stealing or predicting session identifiers

T-P-001.threat: Tampering with process logic or configuration
T-P-001.cause: Insufficient integrity protection for code or configuration
T-P-001.attack: Attacker modifies process code or runtime configuration to alter intended behavior

T-P-002.attack: Attacker exploits memory vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows to manipulate process memory

T-DF-001.cause: Missing integrity protection on data flows
T-DF-001.attack: Attacker intercepts and modifies data in transit between components

T-DF-002.cause: Lack of mutual authentication or secure channel protection
T-DF-002.attack: Attacker positions themselves between communicating parties to intercept and alter transmitted data

T-DS-001.cause: Insufficient access control or integrity protection on storage
T-DS-001.attack: Attacker directly modifies stored data bypassing application-level controls

T-DS-002.cause: Improper input validation and query construction
T-DS-002.attack: Attacker injects malicious input (e.g., SQL) to manipulate or alter stored data

R-EE-001.cause: Lack of reliable logging and non-repudiation mechanisms
R-EE-001.attack: External entity denies having performed an action due to missing or insufficient audit trails

R-P-001.attack: Attacker performs actions that cannot be traced back due to missing or incomplete logs

R-P-002.cause: Lack of protection and integrity controls for logs
R-P-002.attack: Attacker modifies or deletes logs to hide evidence of malicious activity

R-DS-001.cause: Missing audit trail for data changes
R-DS-001.attack: Attacker modifies stored data without leaving traceable evidence

I-P-001.cause: Excessive information exposure in error handling
I-P-001.attack: Detailed error messages reveal sensitive system or internal information

I-P-002.cause: Lack of memory isolation or side-channel protections
I-P-002.attack: Attacker extracts sensitive data from process memory using side-channel techniques

I-DF-001.cause: Unencrypted or weakly protected communication channels
I-DF-001.attack: Attacker intercepts and reads sensitive data transmitted between components

I-DF-002.cause: Lack of traffic obfuscation or metadata protection
I-DF-002.attack: Attacker analyzes communication patterns to infer sensitive information

I-DS-001.cause: Weak access control mechanisms on storage
I-DS-001.attack: Attacker gains unauthorized read access to sensitive stored data

I-DS-002.cause: Improper handling of backups, logs, or temporary files
I-DS-002.attack: Attacker accesses sensitive data through unsecured backups or log files

D-P-001.cause: Improper input validation or error handling
D-P-001.attack: Attacker sends malformed input to trigger crashes or exceptions

D-P-002.cause: Lack of rate limiting or resource controls
D-P-002.attack: Attacker floods the process with requests to exhaust system resources

D-DF-001.attack: Attacker floods network channels to disrupt legitimate communication

D-DS-001.cause: Lack of quotas or storage limits
D-DS-001.attack: Attacker fills storage capacity to block legitimate operations

D-DS-002.cause: Inefficient query handling and lack of resource safeguards
D-DS-002.attack: Attacker executes expensive or long-running queries to lock database resources

E-P-001.cause: Improper input validation and privilege enforcement
E-P-001.attack: Attacker exploits input validation flaws to gain elevated privileges

E-P-002.attack: Attacker bypasses authorization controls to access restricted functionality

E-P-003.cause: Injection vulnerabilities or unsafe execution paths
E-P-003.attack: Attacker injects and executes malicious code within the process context

S-IF-001.cause: Lack of authentication for connected interfaces or devices
S-IF-001.attack: Attacker connects a malicious device impersonating a trusted hardware interface

T-IF-001.cause: Lack of physical protection and tamper resistance
T-IF-001.attack: Attacker manipulates hardware interfaces to alter device behavior or data

R-IF-001.cause: Missing logging for physical interface interactions
R-IF-001.attack: Attacker performs actions via physical interface that cannot be traced

I-IF-001.cause: Unprotected physical or debug interfaces enabling passive monitoring
I-IF-001.attack: Attacker extracts sensitive information using monitoring equipment or side-channel techniques

D-IF-001.cause: Lack of physical protection against deliberate disruption
D-IF-001.attack: Attacker damages or electrically disrupts interface to cause system failure

E-IF-001.cause: Exposed debug or privileged hardware interfaces without access controls
E-IF-001.attack: Attacker uses physical access to debug ports (e.g., JTAG, UART) to gain elevated privileges

E-IF-002.cause: Lack of secure boot or firmware integrity validation
E-IF-002.attack: Attacker manipulates firmware or hardware configuration to gain privileged control over the device

S-SYS-001.threat: System identity spoofing at system boundary
S-SYS-001.cause: Missing or insufficient authentication at the system boundary — communicating parties cannot verify the true system identity
S-SYS-001.attack: Attacker impersonates the system to a connected component, injecting forged responses or commands that are accepted as legitimate

S-SYS-EMB-001.cause: Fieldbus protocols (Modbus, CAN, Profibus) have no built-in authentication — any node can claim any device address
S-SYS-EMB-001.attack: Attacker connects a rogue node to the fieldbus and responds to requests addressed to the legitimate controller, injecting false sensor readings or accepting commands

S-SYS-CLO-001.threat: Cloud service identity spoofing via token theft
S-SYS-CLO-001.cause: Stolen or forged access tokens allow an attacker to impersonate the cloud service towards connected clients
S-SYS-CLO-001.attack: Attacker obtains a service token (e.g., via credential leak or SSRF) and presents it to clients, diverting data flows or issuing unauthorized commands

T-SYS-001.cause: Insufficient integrity protection for system software, firmware, or configuration at rest or during update
T-SYS-001.attack: Attacker modifies system software or configuration to alter system behavior, disable security controls, or introduce a backdoor

T-SYS-EMB-001.cause: Unsigned or weakly authenticated firmware update mechanism — attacker can substitute a malicious firmware image
T-SYS-EMB-001.attack: Attacker delivers a modified firmware image through the update channel (OTA, USB, JTAG) that the device accepts and executes

T-SYS-EMB-002.cause: Debug or programming interface (JTAG, SWD, UART console) is accessible and not locked in production
T-SYS-EMB-002.attack: Attacker connects to the debug interface and directly modifies runtime configuration, memory contents, or persistent parameters

T-SYS-CLO-001.cause: Container images are not cryptographically signed or verified at deployment — a tampered image can be substituted in the registry
T-SYS-CLO-001.attack: Attacker pushes a modified container image to the registry or intercepts the image pull, replacing the legitimate service with a malicious one

T-SYS-MOB-001.cause: Application binary is not protected against repackaging — attacker can inject malicious code and redistribute the modified app
T-SYS-MOB-001.attack: Attacker decompiles the app, injects malicious logic or backdoors, repackages it, and distributes it via sideloading or third-party stores

D-SYS-001.cause: No resource protection or watchdog mechanisms at the system boundary — system can be rendered unavailable by resource exhaustion
D-SYS-001.attack: Attacker floods the system with requests or malformed inputs, exhausting CPU, memory, or network resources until the system becomes unresponsive

D-SYS-EMB-001.threat: Controller resource exhaustion via fieldbus flooding
D-SYS-EMB-001.cause: Controller has no rate limiting or prioritization on the fieldbus — all incoming frames are processed regardless of source or volume
D-SYS-EMB-001.attack: Attacker floods the fieldbus with high-frequency frames addressed to the controller, saturating its communication stack and starving real-time control tasks

D-SYS-SAF-001.threat: Safety system denial of service via invalid safety parameter injection
D-SYS-SAF-001.cause: Safety system accepts parameter updates without strict source validation or rate limiting — invalid parameters can trigger protective shutdown
D-SYS-SAF-001.attack: Attacker injects invalid or out-of-range safety parameters, causing the safety system to trigger an unnecessary protective shutdown and halt the controlled process

E-SYS-001.cause: Insufficient authorization enforcement at the system boundary — an attacker can gain elevated access by exploiting boundary weaknesses
E-SYS-001.attack: Attacker exploits a vulnerability at the system boundary (unauthenticated management interface, weak role separation) to obtain administrative or operator privileges

E-SYS-EMB-001.threat: Privilege escalation via JTAG / SWD debug interface
E-SYS-EMB-001.cause: JTAG or SWD debug interface is not disabled or locked in production — provides full read/write access to processor memory and registers
E-SYS-EMB-001.attack: Attacker connects a debug probe to the JTAG/SWD port, halts the processor, reads security keys from memory, and modifies execution flow to bypass access controls

E-SYS-EMB-002.threat: Privilege escalation via unsigned firmware update
E-SYS-EMB-002.cause: Firmware update process does not enforce cryptographic signature verification — unsigned or weakly signed images are accepted
E-SYS-EMB-002.attack: Attacker crafts a firmware image with elevated privileges or disabled security checks and delivers it through the update channel, permanently compromising the device

E-SYS-CLO-001.cause: Overly permissive IAM policies or missing least-privilege enforcement — a compromised low-privilege identity can reach high-privilege resources
E-SYS-CLO-001.attack: Attacker compromises a low-privilege service account and exploits misconfigured role bindings or wildcard permissions to escalate to administrative access

T-CB-001.threat: Firmware tampering via unlocked debug interface
T-CB-001.cause: Debug interface (JTAG/SWD) is not locked or disabled in production — attacker can access flash memory directly
T-CB-001.attack: Attacker connects a debug probe to the JTAG/SWD port and overwrites firmware with a malicious image that disables security controls or introduces a backdoor

T-CB-002.cause: Firmware readback protection (RDP) or bitstream encryption is not enabled — flash or configuration memory is readable via debug interface
T-CB-002.attack: Attacker reads firmware image or FPGA bitstream via JTAG to extract proprietary algorithms, cryptographic material, or security logic

T-CB-003.threat: Hardware trojan via supply chain compromise
T-CB-003.cause: Chip sourced from unauthorized or grey-market distributor — counterfeit or modified chip may contain hidden functionality
T-CB-003.attack: Attacker substitutes genuine chip with a counterfeit that contains additional logic to exfiltrate data, leak keys, or create a covert channel

I-CB-001.threat: Cryptographic key extraction via side-channel attack
I-CB-001.cause: No side-channel countermeasures implemented — power consumption, timing, or electromagnetic emissions correlate with cryptographic operations
I-CB-001.attack: Attacker measures power traces or EM emissions during cryptographic operations and applies differential power analysis (DPA) to extract private keys

I-CB-002.threat: Firmware information disclosure via unlocked debug interface
I-CB-002.cause: Debug interface allows memory read access without authentication — firmware, configuration, and stored secrets are readable
I-CB-002.attack: Attacker connects to the debug interface and reads flash memory to extract configuration data, credentials, or proprietary firmware

E-CB-001.threat: Privilege escalation via JTAG/SWD debug interface
E-CB-001.cause: JTAG or SWD debug interface is not disabled or locked in production — provides full read/write access to processor memory, registers, and execution flow
E-CB-001.attack: Attacker connects a debug probe, halts the processor, reads security keys from memory, and modifies execution flow to bypass access controls or disable security checks

E-CB-002.threat: Secure Boot bypass via debug interface
E-CB-002.cause: Debug interface remains active in production — allows modification of boot parameters or direct flash overwrite before Secure Boot verification
E-CB-002.attack: Attacker uses debug access to overwrite the bootloader or modify secure boot configuration, enabling unsigned firmware to execute at next power-on

T-P-EMB-001.threat: Embedded process tampering via firmware update channel
T-P-EMB-001.cause: Firmware update mechanism does not enforce cryptographic signature verification — unsigned or modified firmware is accepted
T-P-EMB-001.attack: Attacker delivers a modified firmware image through the update channel (OTA, USB, JTAG) that the device accepts and executes, altering process behavior

E-P-EMB-001.threat: Privilege escalation via embedded debug or service interface
E-P-EMB-001.cause: Debug or service interface is accessible in production without authentication — grants elevated access to process internals
E-P-EMB-001.attack: Attacker uses the debug interface to modify running process state, inject code, or bypass authentication checks at runtime

T-DS-EMB-001.threat: Embedded data store tampering via direct flash access
T-DS-EMB-001.cause: Flash or EEPROM is accessible via debug interface without readback protection — stored data can be modified directly
T-DS-EMB-001.attack: Attacker connects debug probe and overwrites stored configuration, calibration data, or security parameters in flash or EEPROM

I-DS-EMB-001.threat: Sensitive data extraction from embedded storage
I-DS-EMB-001.cause: Flash or EEPROM contains unencrypted sensitive data and is readable via debug interface or physical probing
I-DS-EMB-001.attack: Attacker reads flash memory via JTAG or physical probing to extract API keys, device certificates, or user data stored without encryption

S-P-OT-001.cause: Fieldbus protocols (Modbus, CAN, Profibus) carry no sender authentication — any node can claim any device address
S-P-OT-001.attack: Attacker connects a rogue device to the fieldbus and responds to requests addressed to the legitimate controller, injecting false sensor readings or accepting commands

T-P-OT-001.threat: OT process logic manipulation via unauthenticated protocol
T-P-OT-001.cause: Industrial protocol carries no integrity protection — process parameters can be overwritten without authentication
T-P-OT-001.attack: Attacker injects crafted protocol frames to overwrite process setpoints, force outputs, or modify control logic parameters

D-P-OT-001.threat: OT controller denial of service via fieldbus flooding
D-P-OT-001.cause: Controller has no rate limiting on fieldbus input — all incoming frames are processed regardless of volume
D-P-OT-001.attack: Attacker floods the fieldbus with high-frequency frames, saturating the controller communication stack and starving real-time control tasks

R-SYS-001.threat: System-level repudiation — actions cannot be attributed
R-SYS-001.cause: No tamper-proof audit trail at the system boundary — the system can deny having performed or received actions
R-SYS-001.attack: Attacker exploits missing or insufficient logging to deny malicious actions, making forensic investigation impossible

R-SYS-EMB-001.threat: Repudiation of control actions in embedded or OT system
R-SYS-EMB-001.cause: Embedded controllers and SCADA systems often lack cryptographic audit trails — operator commands and system actions are not non-repudiably logged
R-SYS-EMB-001.attack: Operator or attacker denies having issued a control command (e.g. emergency stop override, setpoint change) because no cryptographically bound audit trail exists
